title: Count High Earners per Department Using Conditional Aggregation
description_markdown: For each `dept_id`, count total employees as `total_emp`, and count how many earn >= 130,000 as `senior_emp` using `SUM(CASE WHEN salary >= 130000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)`. Exclude NULL `dept_id`. Order by `dept_id`.
starter_query:
-- Conditional aggregation with SUM(CASE WHEN ...)
SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS total_emp,
  SUM(CASE WHEN salary >= 130000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS senior_emp
FROM employees
WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ...
solution_query: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS total_emp, SUM(CASE WHEN salary >= 130000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS senior_emp FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dept_id ORDER BY dept_id ASC;
solution_explanation: In MySQL, conditional aggregation is achieved using SUM(CASE WHEN condition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END).
alternative_solutions: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS total_emp, COUNT(CASE WHEN salary >= 130000 THEN 1 END) AS senior_emp FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dept_id ORDER BY dept_id ASC;
common_mistakes: Using PostgreSQL FILTER (WHERE ...) clause which is not supported in MySQL.
dialect_notes: MySQL does not support the FILTER (WHERE ...) clause; use SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) or COUNT(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 END).
hints: Use `SUM(CASE WHEN salary >= 130000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS senior_emp`.
Query: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS total_emp, SUM(CASE WHEN salary >= 130000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS senior_emp FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dept_id ORDER BY dept_id ASC;
